claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a few questions:

**What is your child's name?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. My child's name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'm happy to help you explore your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

To assess whether you qualify, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex is 13 years old.

**Do you live with Alex, or if you don't live with them, are you paying towards their upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex lives with you and is 13 years old, that covers the main residency requirement.

Now I need to check a few more details about your own circumstances to ensure you meet all the eligibility criteria.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Which country do you currently live in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Thank you.

**Are you a Crown servant (someone employed by the UK government in an overseas posting)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Based on the information you've provided, I need to assess your eligibility carefully. You are a UK citizen living in Spain with your 13-year-old child Alex.

According to the Child Benefit rules, you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries. Spain is part of the EU, and there are specific rules about Child Benefit eligibility when living abroad.

**Can you tell me: do you have a right to reside in Spain (for example, through work, self-employment, or residency status)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have residency status in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's useful context.

I need to clarify one more important detail to properly assess your eligibility.

**Are you or have you been paying UK National Insurance contributions, or do you have a connection to the UK through work or employment (either currently or in the past)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I haven't been paying UK National Insurance recently, no.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I have one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex still in school or in any form of education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

Based on all the information you've provided, I now have what I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the rules carefully.

You are a UK citizen living in Spain with your 13-year-old child Alex, who lives with you and is in school. However, according to the UK government's Child Benefit rules, eligibility when living abroad is restricted. 

The rules state that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant. The guidance indicates that Child Benefit eligibility for people living abroad depends on specific circumstances, including having a right to reside in that country and typically maintaining a connection to the UK through work or National Insurance contributions.

Given that you are living in Spain, do not have recent UK National Insurance contributions, and are not a Crown servant, this would typically fall outside the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit while living abroad.

However, to give you the most accurate assessment, I should note that the specific rules for living abroad can be complex and may depend on individual circumstances.

**Have you previously been receiving Child Benefit in the UK before moving to Spain, or is this your first claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This is my first time looking into claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to provide you with my assessment.

conversation.text:
## Summary

I'm afraid that based on your circumstances, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**
- While you and Alex meet the core requirements (you're responsible for Alex and live together), the key issue is that you're currently living in Spain
- The rules do allow for some exceptions for people living abroad, but these are limited to specific situations such as being a Crown servant, which doesn't apply to you
- Additionally, you're not currently paying UK National Insurance contributions, which would typically be needed to maintain eligibility while living abroad

**What you can do:**

If your circumstances change and you return to the UK to live, you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Alternatively, if you have any questions about your specific situation or believe there may be exceptions that apply to you, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly for further guidance.
